To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new method to account for IMs in load-flow calculations is presented and that a seamless transition from load flow to time-domain average powers of IMs is obtained when the reactive power of IMs is not fixed in load-flow calculations.
we developed a new method to initialize time-domain simulations of multiphase induction machines (IM) using load-flow solution.
a new method for modeling induction machines in multiphase power flow calculations was developed and demonstrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
multiphase load flow and initialization of time-domain simulation of IMs.
the following aspects: 1) modeling of IMs in multiphase systems, 2) initialization of time-domain simulation, and 3) load-flow convergence using the Newton method.
the development of a new method for modeling multiphase induction machines in load-flow calculations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiphase load flow with the IMs is a very useful tool in the power system studies, and it can be used for the initialization of time domain simulation.
the proposed method is a powerful and accurate tool for modeling IMs and for initialization of time-domain simulation.
the proposed modeling approach for IMs in multiphase systems allows the load-flow to converge faster and the slip of the machine to be computed accurately.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the multiphase load flow can be used as an initialization for time-domain simulations of induction machines.

the proposed modeling of IMs in load-flow calculations is a general approach that allows accounting for all types of load-flow solutions and initialization of time-domain electromagnetic transient simulations.

we have proposed a novel method to model the induction machine in the load-flow solution, which can be used to solve the load-flow solution of a network containing induction machine(s) and also to initialize the electromagnetic transient simulation of the network containing induction machine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IM slip is a variable in the load-flow solution and it is calculated iteratively.
the IM can be modeled in the load-flow calculation with the slip of the machine as a variable, and the reactive power of the machine is not fixed.
the load flow can be used to initialize time-domain simulations of IMs.
